restrictions.text: RSMo 306.325 (canoes, kayaks and similar easily-tipped craft, and inner tubes, carrying food or drink): no glass beverage containers on the vessel within the banks of navigable waterways; food and drink must be in a cooler or similar non-glass container sealed so contents cannot spill; carry and affix to the vessel a closable bag or container for trash, and carry all trash out to a lawful disposal place. Violation is a class C misdemeanor.
RSMo 577.070: littering (throwing or depositing glass, cans, trash or other refuse on land or in waters) is a crime in Missouri. Pack out all trash.

RSMo 306.220: each person under the age of seven on board any watercraft on Missouri waters must wear a USCG-approved personal flotation device (exceptions in the statute). RSMo 306.100: watercraft must carry a USCG-approved personal flotation device for each person on board.

Stream access (Missouri DNR pub 1350): "There is no state statutory right to access streams or lakes." "Access to a stream must be from public property or with permission from the landowner. In Missouri on navigable streams, the landowner generally owns to the low water edge." The right to float does not allow trespass on private property, so banks and gravel bars beside private land may be private — launch and take out only at public accesses.
restrictions.evidenceType: state agency publication (DNR pub 1350) + MDC trespass page

restrictions.text: Ozark National Scenic Riverways: at high river levels the park implements temporary river closures for both commercial and non-commercial vessels; closure information is posted on the park's Facebook page by 9 a.m., and non-motorized vessels on the rivers during a closure are in violation and can be cited.
restrictions.evidenceType: NPS news release (archived 2020) + NPS conditions page

restrictions.text: ONSR superintendent's compendium: the compendium sets maximum motor horsepower by river reach; check the current compendium table before running a motor.
ONSR compendium: the compendium regulates the practice of lashing vessels together and restricts alcoholic beverages in designated areas and periods; check the current compendium text.

ONSR access rules (2020 release): Waymeyer serves non-commercial floaters only; Pin Oak is limited to NPS-permitted commercial operators Friday–Sunday; the Chilton Creek boat ramp is for motorized vessels only; Raftyard is for commercial and non-commercial tube use only. These sites are pending (no usable coordinate) in this package.
restrictions.evidenceType: NPS news release (archived 2020; may be outdated)

restrictions.text: ONSR (2020 release): the Round Spring lower river access and boat ramp were severely damaged by flooding; vehicle access was repaired for non-motorized launching, and motorized boats should use the middle landing near Group Campsite 9.
restrictions.evidenceType: NPS news release (archived 2020; may be outdated)

restrictions.text: NPS paddle pages: "portions are only navigable during certain times due to low river levels." Check river levels and closures before departing.
NPS-authorized outfitters (concessioners) rent canoes, kayaks, rafts and tubes and run shuttles inside the park; NPS: "no charge for private vessels."

Mark Twain NF forest order, Eleven Point Wild and Scenic River zone: motorboats over 25 horsepower prohibited; possessing glass beverage or food containers prohibited within the designated boundary (except Greer Campground and Picnic Area, Riverton Picnic Area and private lands); the public may not enter private land within the scenic river easement.

USFS (Thomasville River Access): "This section of river can usually be floated March through June. Motorized boats are not recommended." Some spots require walking or portages where the river is not deep, particularly in drought season.

restrictions.text: MDC conservation areas and accesses (3 CSR 10-11): department areas are open 4:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. daily with exceptions (for example fishing and boating access); area-specific rules, including where boats may not be left unattended overnight, are on each MDC area page and in the regulation.
restrictions.evidenceType: Missouri Code of State Regulations (3 CSR 10-11)

restrictions.text: USACE Clearwater Lake (Little Rock District): Clearwater is "operated primarily for flood control", so Black River flow below the dam depends on dam operation; River Road Park sits on the Black River just below the dam. Check the USGS gauge before floating.
restrictions.evidenceType: USACE page (fetched with the web-fetch tool; scripted fetch 403)

restrictions.text: Lower Missouri River (water-trail safety page): large barges travel the channel marked by navigation markers and cannot steer around canoes or kayaks — move to the side and wait; USACE wing dams/L-dikes along the entire lower river can create turbulence and strong currents best avoided by small craft.

USFS (Slabtown Recreation Area): "Between Ross Bridge and East Gate, a 12-mile float, you will be floating through Fort Leonard Wood. Ross Bridge will be the last take-out before you float through Fort Leonard Wood."

restrictions.text: Missouri State Parks — Meramec State Park page: the Meramec in the park is "not recommended for propeller boats"; state park rules apply inside park boundaries.
